text:
maya: Thanks everyone for coming to the runtime roadmap Q&A — appreciate the good questions. Recording + slides are up: https://redwood.internal/drive/runtime-qna :wave:

kevin: Quick recap from my side — kernel work is split into three pillars: 1) baseline perf and memory fixes (rolling out next 4 weeks), 2) fused attention & optimized matmul kernels (targeting late Q2 / early Q3), 3) quantized fast-path + int8 kernels (Q4). Expect ~1.5-2x throughput on medium-length chat loads after pillar 2.

sam: Will the new kernels require model changes or API changes?

kevin: No API surface changes. It's all under the serving runtime. Models keep the same checkpoints. We will expose a couple of runtime flags in the Console for advanced tuning but defaults keep backward compatibility.

anya: For Dedicated customers, what's the canary/rollback plan?

kevin: Canary rollout per pool + per-model. Canary percentage starts small (1-2% traffic), health checks (latency, error rate) run for 30m. Auto-rollback if SLO break. We'll publish the exact gating rules in the rollout doc next week.

ryan: For batching/caching: are there recommended defaults we should move org-wide? We see a lot of customers with tiny batch sizes causing cost overhead.

kevin: Yes — proposed defaults (draft) are in the RFC. Short version: increase max_batch_tokens to 4096, enable prefix KV caching for chat routes, and prefer adaptive batching based on 95th percentile latency window. Small snippet I shared in the meeting:

```
runtime:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  prefix_cache: enabled
  adaptive_batching:
    target_p95_ms: 120
  hot_routes:
    - /chat
    - /generate
```

kevin: We'll add a migration tool in the Console so orgs can preview cost impact before switching.

olivia: I can own the migration checklist for public customers — will sync with SRE and Support.

maya: Amazing — thanks Olivia. Can you create a short checklist doc and assign owners?

olivia: Yep, I'll create the checklist and ping here when it's ready.

sam: Any numerical goal for end-to-end latency improvements with combined batching + kernels?

kevin: Ballpark: 15-30% median latency reduction on chat workloads with adaptive batching + KV cache; up to 50% tail reduction once fused kernels land. All numbers depend on seq length distribution. We'll publish benchmark runs with the release.

deploy-bot: Recording uploaded to drive: https://redwood.internal/drive/runtime-qna/recording.mp4 :white_check_mark:

maya: Follow-ups for the owners: Kevin to publish rollout gating rules by next Tue; Olivia to produce migration checklist; Ryan to draft console preview UI for migration; Sam to help validate benchmarks with sample workloads. I'll consolidate and send assignments after lunch. :thumbsup:
